crime_highlights: The appellant was convicted of the following 15 offences: criminal negligence causing death; fail to remain at the scene of the collision
rationale_highlights: The trial judge took into account the very few factors that were helpful to the appellant, including his Indigenous offender status
note: Appeal court says mitigating factors were overwhelmed; no clear reduction for Indigenous status.

crime_highlights: the appellant punched her twice in the back of the head, knocking her out
The appellant hit and kicked Mr. Gill until he fell to the floor
Her next memory is waking up in hospital with numerous severe injures
the appellant continued beating his mother in her bedroom, where forensics later identified a great deal of blood spatter
rationale_highlights: Gladue reports were created in order to address systemic injustice that uniquely affects Indigenous offenders, and which leads to overrepresentation in the criminal justice system
A long delay undermines the purpose of the Gladue report by creating another level of unfairness
The delay was caused by a failure to provide adequate services to a vulnerable segment of society
note: Reduction is for Charter delay; court never says Gladue factors reduced culpability.

crime_highlights: convicted of impaired driving, dangerous driving, failing to stop while being pursued by the police, and driving while disqualified
rationale_highlights: The trial judge carefully reviewed the Gladue report and took into account the systemic factors that contributed to his offending
He made specific reference to links between the appellant’s alcohol use and events in the appellant’s personal life, noting the appellant’s moral blameworthiness was reduced
We see no basis for interfering with the sentence imposed
note: Appeal court endorses trial judge finding of reduced moral blameworthiness.
